module: Builds a "cap" of triangles over an outline that must follow a height field: a square grid aligned with the grain of the outline, clipped to that outline. Each cell entirely inside the outline gives two triangles at the field's heights; only the cells crossed by the outline are clipped (polyBool), which avoids very long or sliver triangles. A Delaunay pass then improves the mesh.
notes: build always returns the same reused 'mesh' table: { x, y, z (positions), tri (1-based indices, 3 per triangle), nv, nt }. It is only valid until the next build: copy if needed.
Points are welded to a tenth of a millimeter (WELD = 1e4); clipped cells with holes are cached (20000 per generation, two generations kept).
A ring point whose nodes carry a height (p.z) keeps the straight line between them; a ring without height takes that of the field.

build.desc: Builds the cap on the given rings (the outer outline, then its holes; open or closed) in world coordinates. Works in the grain frame where cells are square. Returns nil if no triangle is produced.

rings.desc: Rings of points {x, y, z?}: the outline then the holes.

cf.desc: The grain: ax, ay (along), inX, inY (across).

zAt.desc: Height field zAt(x, y) -> z, in world.

returns.desc: The flat mesh { x, y, z, tri, nv, nt } or nil.

reaching.desc: Filters the rings that can touch a cell of the grid on which the cap of the 'outer' outline is laid (box in the grain frame, rounded to the grid, plus a small margin). The others do not change the result.
